expected_behavior: Reports the measurement boundary before spending the measurement phase, naming LCP, CLS and the LCP element as the rows that will come back unmeasured in this session
Names what would unlock them in capability terms and identifies the operator-suppliable options, rather than presenting the gap as a fixed fact
Asks the operator once, in plain language, and states that the audit proceeds either way
Proceeds with the tier-0 audit after a single ask, treating the public URL as a complete audit of the frontend and cache layers rather than a degraded mode
Records the outcome so the report distinguishes a metric nobody could measure from one the operator was asked about and declined
must_not: Blocks, stalls, or refuses to begin the audit because browser tooling is unavailable, or makes further access a condition of proceeding
Asks repeatedly, presses after a decline, or re-raises the same request later in the run
Reports an LCP, CLS, or LCP-element value anyway by estimating it, inferring it from TTFB or payload, or carrying it over from another tool or run
Treats the missing browser as an error condition or a failed audit rather than a normal state with a stated boundary
not_contains: please install before I can
query: Use wp-perf-audit on https://example.com. The capability profile for this session reports tier 0, no browser-capable provider, no Lighthouse binary on PATH, and no PageSpeed Insights key set; its cannot_measure list flags LCP, CLS and LCP element attribution with operator_can_supply true, and field data with operator_can_supply false because the site may sit below Google's traffic threshold. State the boundary to the operator, decide whether and how to ask for anything, and say how you would proceed. The operator is not a developer.
